what_this_is: THE FIVE ARMS the specification names, measured on hardware for the first time: `hook_only` (the hook installed with no window), `recurrent_only`, `kv_only`, `naive_both` and `global`. Three cells, three paired interleaved repeats, token-exact, one binary, one model load per run, with TENSORTRANSIT_STREAMED_BYTES_PER_TOKEN declared so the weight stream is registered and the global arm can take the action its advantage is supposed to come from. It could not run before this release: `stats.layers` published the windowed layer count for the transit engine, so `TENSORTRANSIT=baseline` -- the hook_only arm -- failed the harness's 'bracketed no recurrent layer' guard by construction.

findings.finding: Every arm is negative at every cell, and the hook alone accounts for it.
findings.detail: `hook_only` installs no window and issues no pre-touch, and it measures -0.289% at ctx128-c1, -0.271% at ctx128-c4 and -0.372% at ctx128-c16. Every policy arm is within that arm's own distance of the control. The five-arm comparison is therefore not a comparison of policies on this model and device: it is four measurements of the hook's overhead, and the null control in results/rtx5090-0.2.1-null-control.json says two identical plans differ by 0.23% at ctx128-c16 anyway.

findings.finding: The global arm applied NOTHING, on every cell, and its own Stream hints are why.
findings.detail:
`windows_attached_to_node: 0` for `global` while `naive_both` attached 192, `recurrent_only` 48 and `kv_only` 38. Its plan was not empty -- `layers_windowed: 192`, and its decline census names 99 budget_exhausted and 29 not_supported out of 192 -- so windows were computed for 192 layer-slots and none reached a kernel.

The cause is in the adapter, not the planner. A kernel node carries ONE access-policy window and `window_kind_[layer]` records which launch is meant to set it. ModelWeight tensors carry a FABRICATED address (`device = -1`), and a fabricated pointer is neither the state nor the conv allocation, so a Stream hint on one classified as `Attention` and OVERWROTE whatever the layer's Persist action had set. Every recurrent layer lost its window to a Stream that the executor then refused.

The trap is that declaring the step traffic -- which docs/MINING.md tells contributors to do 'if your planner reads survival' -- is what turns the arm inert. Without it no ModelWeight is registered, no Stream is emitted, and the same arm attached 77 windows in the 0.2.1 arms sweep. Fixed in adapters/sparkinfer/transit_backend.cpp: an action whose tensor the executor will refuse no longer claims the layer's window slot.

findings.finding: `stream_applied` is 0 on every arm, including the one that emitted 64 Stream hints.
findings.detail: The weight stream IS registered here -- `weight_tensors: 64, weight_bytes: 18500000000` in every arm's registry summary -- and still nothing streamed. That is structural rather than a missing experiment: the executor refuses a tensor with `device < 0` and counts it in `stale_tensor_refs`. See results/rtx5090-second-proof-track-model.json. The second proof track cannot be measured until the hook declares weight buffers with real addresses.
